info.label: XL Recordings
info.desc: In Rainbows is the seventh studio album by the English alternative rock band Radiohead. It was first released on October 10, 2007 as a digital download that customers could order for whatever price they saw fit, followed by a standard CD release in most countries during the last week of 2007. The album was released in North America on January 1, 2008. In Rainbows was Radiohead's first release after the end of their contract with EMI and the end of the longest gap between studio albums in their career. "In Rainbows" was recorded in London, Somerset, Wiltshire, and Oxfordshire with .

podcast.body: After *Hail to the Thief* in July 2003, a new Radiohead album did not appear until October 10, 2007 — a gap of over four years. Thom Yorke later admitted that in the spring of 2005 he was suffering writer's block caused by panic attacks triggered by his fears over global warming. He acknowledged being obsessed by the subject to the point where he could not work on new music. Once he immersed himself in researching the problem and found some framework for solutions, the block lifted and he was able to write again. "This was something that was obsessing me and creating a writer's block."

podcast.body: Following its initial direct-to-fan digital release, "In Rainbows" was conventionally released through XL Recordings. The album achieved total sales of over 3 million copies, including nearly 2 million physical sales, demonstrating its broad commercial success beyond the experimental digital release. "More people bought the album when it was released conventionally through Excel recordings. Total sales seemed to be somewhere north of 3 million copies, including nearly 2 million physical sales."

podcast.body: For the special edition of *In Rainbows*, Radiohead included fragments of old, degraded electromagnetic master tapes from their past recordings. This unusual inclusion was a direct response to the tapes deteriorating and being slated for disposal, offering fans a physical piece of their vanishing audio history. "cuando reídiójecido la edición especial del donde está del ultimo disco del namón se fue en nos regalaba un trozo de cinta electromagnética de sus grabaciones antiguas porque ya se habían degradado tanto y se estaban borrando que dijo me la vamos a tirar la basura pues la regalamos."

podcast.body: Launched in October 2007 with a revolutionary "tip jar" approach, allowing fans to pay whatever they wanted for a digital download, including nothing. This risky strategy proved highly successful, with Radiohead estimating they received more net revenue from it than from their previous seven albums with EMI. When physically released through independent labels, it sold an additional million copies. "In October of 2007, radio head launched their In Rainbows album with its famous tip jar approach."

podcast.body: Radiohead fans identified an elaborate numerical pattern connecting the two albums over a decade apart. *In Rainbows* has 10 tracks, contains 10 letters in its title, was released on October 10 (the 10th day of the 10th month), was made available on an alleged 10 download servers, was announced on October 1 (10 days before release) via 10 cryptic fan messages each using the letter X (Roman numeral 10). Some fans believe the albums are meant to be listened to together by interleaving tracks — starting with "Airbag" from *OK Computer*, then "15 Step" from *In Rainbows*, alternating, with each song cross-faded by 10 seconds. A listener named Kevin applied the golden mean (1.618/divine proportion) to the total length of *In Rainbows* in seconds, producing a timestamp landing at 2 minutes 49 seconds into "Reckoner" — a major crescendo where Tom's vocals shift "from U to In Rainbows." A mole inside Radiohead reportedly confirmed Thom Yorke was "most amused" watching the theorists at work. "It sent chills down my spine."

podcast.body: Released digitally on October 10, 2007, this seventh album by Radiohead was initially offered on a radical "pay what you want" model directly to fans, bypassing traditional record label distribution. Despite 62% of downloaders paying nothing, those who did paid an average of $6, resulting in an overall average of $2.26 per download, and earning Radiohead more from digital sales than all their previous six albums combined. "On October 1st, 2007, the group announced that their new album in Rainbows, their 7th, would be available on October 10th, 2007, and it would be offered for free."

podcast.body: Released in 2007, this album marked Radiohead's most significant contribution to the indie world after their departure from major labels. They independently managed all aspects, including recording, manufacturing, distribution, and pioneered a "tip jar approach" to pricing, allowing fans to pay what they wished online, alongside a deluxe physical set for a fixed price. Despite many choosing to pay nothing, the band reportedly earned more from *In Rainbows* than any other release in their career, including *OK Computer*. "The biggest contribution Radiohead made to the indie world came with the In Rainbows album in 2007. They handled everything themselves, recording, manufacturing, distribution, and this is important. Pricing. In Rainbows pioneered the tip jar approach. Here's the record. You can get various forms of it online, and you can pay anything you want for it. Oh, and there was a deluxe set that sold for some serious cash as well. Even though thousands chose to pay nothing for the record, it was reported that Radiohead ended up making more money from In Rainbows than they did from any other release in their career, and that includes okay computer."

podcast.body: The album was completed by July 2007, amidst the band's dispute with EMI. Radiohead decided to retain full ownership, including publishing, masters, and copyright. It was secretly announced on October 1, 2007, by guitarist Jonny Greenwood on their website Dead Air Space, stating it would be released in 10 days. The album became available on October 10, 2007, at inrainbows.com, featuring a unique "pay-what-you-want" model where fans determined the price, only paying a mandatory credit card processing fee of 45 pence (about 90 cents USD). The songs were 160 kbps, DRM-free, and distributed via a private network to handle anticipated heavy traffic. While many downloaded it for free, only two out of five visitors paid more than the minimum fee, with an average payment of four pounds (about eight dollars). Despite this, the band netted millions in pure profits, and in December 2007, a premium disc box was released for 40 pounds, including the CD, a bonus CD, digital photos, artwork, and 180-gram vinyl. The album's release was tied to a "Theory of Ten" with various numerical coincidences. It generated approximately £3 million in pure profits and sold 3 million copies across all formats, becoming the biggest-selling vinyl record of 2008. "The new album is finished, and it's coming out in 10 days. We called it In Rainbows."
